# rust-fetch

> Resilient HTTP client for JavaScript and TypeScript (npm package `rust-fetch`), with a Rust core compiled to WebAssembly that behaves the same in browsers, Web Workers and Node.js 20+. It adds what `fetch()` lacks: typed errors, per-attempt timeouts, retries with backoff, interceptors, upload and download progress, streaming, Server-Sent Events and newline-delimited JSON (for LLM streaming APIs), and WebSockets with reconnection. Also usable as a Rust crate.

Use rust-fetch when you want `fetch()` plus production policy (timeouts, retries, error handling) in one client, the same in the browser and in Node.js. Prefer `undici.request()` for maximum raw throughput in Node.js only, and native `fetch()` when bundle size matters most (rust-fetch adds about 188 KB brotli to a browser bundle).

## Install and set up

```js
// npm install rust-fetch
import { WasmClient } from 'rust-fetch';          // Node.js: ready on import
// Browsers and bundlers: import init, { WasmClient } from 'rust-fetch'; await init();

const client = new WasmClient({
  baseUrl: 'https://api.example.com/v1', // relative URLs are appended to it
  headers: { authorization: 'Bearer …' }, // sent with every request
  timeoutMs: 10_000,                      // per attempt, including the body; default 30000; 0 disables
  retries: 3,                             // or { maxRetries, initialDelayMs, maxDelayMs, multiplier, retryOn, retryOnNetworkError, retryOnTimeout, retryNonIdempotent }
});
```

## Requests

- `client.get(url, options?)`, `head`, `delete`: no body
- `client.post(url, { body, ...options })`, `put`, `patch`; `client.fetch(url, { method, body, ...options })`
- `client.post_json(url, body, options?)`, `put_json`, `patch_json`: always JSON
- TypeScript: `client.get<User>('/users/42')` resolves to `HttpResponse<User>` (the type isn't validated at runtime)
- Bodies: string, `Uint8Array`/`ArrayBuffer`/`DataView`, `Blob`/`File`, `FormData` (multipart), `URLSearchParams`, or any value sent as JSON
- Options: `headers`, `params` (query string), `timeoutMs`, `responseType` (`'auto' | 'json' | 'text' | 'binary' | 'stream' | 'ndjson'`), `signal` (AbortSignal), `onDownloadProgress({ loaded, total })`, `onUploadProgress({ loaded, total })`, `redirect`, `maxRedirects`
- WebSockets through a proxy (Node.js): `client.websocket(url, { dispatcher: new ProxyAgent(proxyUrl) })` with `ProxyAgent` from the `undici` package
- Security: credentials are dropped on cross-origin redirects; CR/LF in headers rejected; only http(s); set `allowAbsoluteUrls: false` with a `baseUrl` so user-supplied paths can't redirect requests (and the client's `Authorization`) to another host
- `maxResponseBytes` (client or per request; `null` per request for none): limit on the decompressed body, checked against Content-Length, counted while reading and while decompressing (decompression bombs never expand); rejects with a `NetworkError` carrying `maxResponseBytes`
- `maxPendingRequests` (client option, every transport): refuse a request at once while the client has this many started and not settled, in flight or waiting (retries included; streams until their headers); rejects with a `NetworkError` carrying `maxPendingRequests`, nothing sent
- `maxLineBytes` (client, per `ndjson` request or `events()` stream; `null` for none): longest line in UTF-8 bytes without its line break, checked before buffering; earlier lines are delivered, then the stream errors with a `NetworkError` carrying `maxLineBytes` and closes (events aren't reconnected); SSE `data:` lines are checked one at a time, not an event's total
- `websocket()` `maxQueuedMessages` / `maxQueuedBytes`: limit what `send()` queues before the connection opens or while reconnecting; past either, `send()` throws a `NetworkError` carrying the limit and doesn't queue
- `allowPrivateNetwork: false` (Node.js, client or per request): SSRF protection; blocks loopback/private/link-local/metadata/reserved addresses, checked on resolved addresses at connect time and on every redirect
- Node.js proxies (client option): `proxy: 'env'` (`HTTPS_PROXY`/`HTTP_PROXY`/`NO_PROXY`; also on with `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1`) or `proxy: 'http://user:pass@host:3128'`; HTTPS via CONNECT tunnels
- Browser `fetch()` options (client or per request; ignored in Node.js): `credentials`, `mode` (`'no-cors'` resolves with an opaque `status: 0` response), `cache`, `keepalive`, `priority`, `referrer`, `referrerPolicy`, `integrity`
- Redirects (client or per request): `redirect: 'follow'` (default, up to `maxRedirects`, default 20), `'manual'` (resolves with the 3xx and its `location` header, `ok: false`; in browsers an opaque response with `status: 0`), `'error'` (rejects with a `NetworkError`)

Resolves (2xx only) to `{ status, statusText, ok, url, headers, body }`. With `responseType: 'auto'`, `body` is parsed JSON for `application/json` and `*+json`, a string for text types, a `Uint8Array` otherwise, `null` when empty.

## Errors

Every failure rejects with an `Error` whose `kind` (and `name`) is one of:
- `HttpError`: non-2xx; has `status`, `statusText`, `body` (response text)
- `TimeoutError`: an attempt exceeded `timeoutMs`; has `timeoutMs`
- `NetworkError`: DNS, connection, TLS, CORS, truncated body, or a WebSocket failure
- `CancelledError`: the `signal` aborted
- `InvalidInputError`: bad URL, header, option or body, before sending; has `parameter`
- `ParseError`: `responseType: 'json'` and the body isn't JSON
- `JsInteropError`: unexpected JS/Wasm conversion failure

Retries are off by default. When on, POST and PATCH aren't retried unless `retryNonIdempotent: true`; `Retry-After` (seconds) is honoured; only `retryOn` statuses (default 408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504), network errors and timeouts are retried. A request that fails every attempt rejects with the last attempt's error.

## Interceptors

```js
client.addRequestInterceptor((request) => { request.headers.authorization = `Bearer ${token}`; });
client.addResponseInterceptor((response) => response, (error) => { throw error; });
// both return an id for client.ejectInterceptor(id); client.clearInterceptors() removes all
```

## Streaming and progress

```js
const res = await client.get('/export.csv', { responseType: 'stream' }); // res.body is a ReadableStream<Uint8Array>
await client.post('/upload', { body: formData, onUploadProgress: ({ loaded, total }) => {} });
```

Upload progress uses `XMLHttpRequest` in browsers (cross-origin requests are preflighted) and the `node:http` transport in Node.js.

## Server-Sent Events and streaming JSON

```js
// SSE in browsers and Node.js, any method/headers/body; e.g. an OpenAI-compatible streaming API
const stream = client.events('/v1/chat/completions', {
  method: 'POST',
  body: { model, messages, stream: true },
  messageType: 'json',        // data parsed as JSON; stops at `data: [DONE]` (option `end`)
  // reconnect: true          // default for GET: resends Last-Event-ID, honours `retry:`
});
for await (const { event, data, id } of stream) console.log(data.choices[0].delta.content);  // a slow loop pauses reading at 64 queued events (backpressure)
// or callbacks: client.events(url, { onEvent, onError, onOpen, onReconnect, onClose }); stream.close()

// Newline-delimited JSON (e.g. Ollama): one parsed value per line
const res = await client.post('/api/generate', { body: { model, prompt }, responseType: 'ndjson' });
for await (const chunk of res.body) console.log(chunk.response);
```

## WebSockets

```js
const socket = client.websocket('/live', {          // https base URL → wss://…/live
  params: { room: 'blue' },
  messageType: 'json',                              // 'auto' (default) or 'json'
  reconnect: true,                                  // or a number, or { maxRetries, initialDelayMs, maxDelayMs, multiplier }
  onMessage: (message) => {},
  onError: (error) => {},                           // typed errors, as for requests
});
await socket.opened;                                // rejects if it never connects
socket.sendJson({ type: 'subscribe' });             // socket.send(string | ArrayBuffer | typed array | Blob)
socket.close();                                     // stops reconnecting
const { code, reason, wasClean } = await socket.closed;
```

Needs a built-in `WebSocket`: browsers and Node.js 22+ (Node.js 20 with `--experimental-websocket`). Handshake `headers` work in Node.js only.
